title: Turbo Tenant · Engineering Atlas
summary: A source-linked map of the tenant host, plugin modules, storefront, data declarations, and request boundaries. Start with the architecture, then follow individual routes and workflows.

Failures are summarized at their actual stage. A first authenticated delivery address is saved before order placement; a failed address save prevents the order request.

diagrams.title: Meta integration · Pixel, Conversions API and catalog
diagrams.description: Source-reviewed component view of the meta-marketing plugin. Storefront code emits vendor-neutral commerce events; only the meta-marketing frontend plugin talks to the Pixel and the relay endpoint. Purchase is server-authoritative: it is never relayed and is sent by queued jobs from order events. Browser and server copies share an event_id so Meta deduplicates them. Delivery to the live Graph API has not been exercised by this atlas.

diagrams.title: Meta Purchase · COD at placement, online after payment
diagrams.description: Reviewed control flow for the Purchase conversion. COD orders are finalized and reported inside the placement request; online orders are reported only when the payment state machine transitions to completed. The job skips POS orders, disabled CAPI and already-sent orders, writes every attempt to meta_capi_events, retries 5xx/connection errors and stops on 4xx.
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
 actor Customer
 participant SPA as Storefront hooks
 participant Place as PlaceOrderService
 participant Capture as CaptureOrderTrackingContext
 participant Resp as PurchaseTrackingResponseContributor
 participant Job as SendMetaPurchaseEvent (queue)
 participant Meta as Meta Pixel and Conversions API
 Customer->>SPA: Place order
 SPA->>Place: POST /api/orders/place
 Place->>Capture: OrderCreated (sync)
 Note over Capture: Store fbp/fbc cookies, IP, user agent, source URL. Skip POS
 alt Offline / COD
  Place->>Job: OrderFinalized, dispatch with event_time now
  Place-->>Resp: success
  Resp-->>SPA: tracking with purchase_event_id, value, contents
  SPA->>Meta: Pixel Purchase, eventID purchase.order
 else Online payment
  Place-->>Resp: success and checkout URL
  Resp-->>SPA: tracking
  SPA->>SPA: keep tracking in sessionStorage
  SPA->>Customer: Redirect to gateway
  Note over Place: Payment webhook, PaymentStateMachine completed
  Place->>Job: OrderPaymentCompleted, dispatch with event_time now
  SPA->>Meta: Callback page when paid, Pixel Purchase once
 end
 Job->>Job: Skip if CAPI off, POS, or purchase already sent
 Job->>Meta: Graph API event, hashed user_data, same event_id
 alt 2xx
  Job->>Job: log sent, mark purchase_sent_at
 else 4xx
  Job->>Job: log failed, admin can retry
 else 5xx or connection error
  Job->>Job: log failed and throw, queue retries 10s to 1h
 end

diagrams.title: Meta catalog feed · request to rows
diagrams.description: Reviewed flow of the catalog export. Prices mirror CartPriceCalculator so the advertised price equals the charged price (variant price as-is; product discount only when below base). Products without an image are skipped; inactive products are listed as out of stock. The feed is generated on every fetch, so it is never stale; it deliberately avoids the Laravel cache because tenancy's cache bootstrapper needs a taggable store and the app runs on the database store.

observations.title: Schema provenance requires care
observations.description: The tenant baseline and plugin directories both contain table declarations. This atlas retains every create declaration and change operation. It does not assume lexical order across independently activated plugin migration sets, and does not claim these declarations equal a tenant’s live schema.

observations.title: Panel admission and plugin visibility
observations.description: User::canAccessPanel requires is_admin for the admin panel and returns true for other panel IDs. Authentication middleware still applies to panels. BelongsToPlugin checks plugin activation for resource access and navigation. These are distinct controls; role and policy completeness has not been tested.

observations.title: Resource ownership is enforced in more than one form
observations.description: Address update/delete use AddressPolicy ownership checks via Gate::authorize. Customer order queries constrain user_id and return 404 for unavailable details. Route middleware alone does not capture these restrictions. Order history filters validate order and payment status, then constrain the authenticated customer query before pagination.

observations.title: Browser routes and server routes are separate
observations.description: React declares /orders/:id/payment/callback while Laravel also registers a callback handler for that URL shape. The atlas records both declarations; a browser navigation can reach the server handler before React routing. Runtime navigation behavior has not been exercised.

observations.title: Registration does not establish tenant activation
observations.description: All discovered plugin providers are registered during application setup. TenantPlugin status controls tenant boot, contributions, route gates, and activation-gated event handlers. A route being registered does not establish that a tenant can execute it.

observations.title: Coupon and payment request call sites align with registered /api prefixes
observations.description: Coupon validation call sites (/api/coupons/validate), payment status, and Kashier configuration hooks use their registered /api-prefixed paths under the shared client baseURL /. Runtime checkout and Kashier gateway behavior remain subject to tenant configuration.

observations.title: Storefront document hydration and deferred screens
observations.description: The tenant HTML shell serializes BootstrapController output with Laravel Js::from. Active BootstrapContributor implementations may add query_data entries. The home document includes catalog sections/categories and combo packages from shared StorefrontData readers; hero banners are contributed through the same activation gate. The browser seeds tenant, auth and plugin React Query caches before mounting. API endpoints remain available for later fetches. Account and selected plugin screens load through React.lazy under the router Suspense boundary. This is source-reviewed startup behavior; tenant schema equivalence and all production cache configurations remain unverified.

observations.title: Static delivery and startup styles
observations.description: The local PHP router serves versioned Vite assets with negotiated gzip for text assets, immutable caching and representation-specific ETags; Apache has corresponding compression/cache declarations. This does not establish other production web-server configurations. Tenant theme CSS is generated by ThemeCssBuilder from the validated `theme` store setting (hex colors and a fixed radius map only) and embedded in the document with closing style tags escaped; Tailwind color utilities resolve through `@theme inline` to those CSS variables. Storefront Tailwind sources exclude compiled views and admin-only templates. The cart bootstrap contributor exposes cart_count only; full cart data is fetched by the existing useCart hook through GET /api/cart when the header cart mounts. The document does not seed the cart query cache.

observations.title: Inline production styles and opcode-cached local server
observations.description: Production storefront CSS is an explicit Vite entry whose compiled content is embedded in the HTML; the development hot-server path still uses Vite stylesheet loading. This trades roughly 17 KiB of compressed document bytes for removing a blocking CSS request. serve:fast extends the local Laravel server launcher, enabling OPcache where the extension is available, validating timestamps on every request and preserving the existing tenant router. It changes neither global PHP configuration nor production server configuration. Warm local measurements verify reduced boot latency; cold process startup remains slower.

observations.title: POS delivery audit and replay boundaries
observations.description: POS delivery and attempt tables are tenant-scoped migration declarations. Manual sends and reviews require administrator and active-addon checks. Counts cover recorded attempts; historical attempts are not reconstructed. Unknown POST outcomes require branch verification, while delayed/stale generations cannot overwrite newer delivery state. Default database jobs use explicit central storage and carry the tenant context. Tests use fake POS responses; remote orderNumber deduplication and deployment worker availability remain unverified. Schema declarations do not establish a live tenant schema. The POS Filament plugin registers the delivery-history Livewire component before tenancy starts; tenant/addon/admin checks still control visibility and data access.

observations.title: Meta Purchase and funnel events
observations.description: meta-marketing listens to OrderCreated synchronously to store fbp/fbc, client IP, user agent and source URL; OrderFinalized (offline/COD, dispatched during placement) and OrderPaymentCompleted (online) queue SendMetaPurchaseEvent after commit with deterministic event id purchase.{order_id}, skipping POS orders. The placement response gains a tracking block that the storefront uses for the browser Pixel Purchase with the same event id; online orders fire it only after the payment status reports paid. Other storefront events go through the core commerce event bus to the Pixel and are mirrored to POST /api/meta/events. Delivery to Meta has not been exercised against the live Graph API.

observations.title: Meta catalog feed and secrets
observations.description: The catalog feed routes are reachable without a session but return 404 unless the catalog is enabled and the path token matches (hash_equals). The Conversions API access token is stored encrypted in tenant settings, never sent to the storefront bootstrap, and excluded from the delivery log payload. _fbp/_fbc are excluded from cookie encryption so the server can read Meta's browser cookies.

observations.title: Meta content ID scheme
observations.description: Pixel events, Conversions API payloads and the catalog feed use one ID format so events match catalog items: "{product_id}" for products without variants, "{product_id}-{variant_id}" for variants (item_group_id = product id). ViewContent before a variant is chosen uses content_type product_group with the product id. Backend MetaContentId and frontend metaContentId must change together; the MetaDiagnostics ID consistency check compares recent order items with the feed.

observations.title: Operating the Meta integration
observations.description: Per tenant: activate meta-marketing (tenant:plugin:activate migrates meta_order_tracking and meta_capi_events) and keep a queue worker running. Admin Settings tab "تسويق ميتا (Meta)" holds the Pixel ID (stored under the legacy facebook_app_id key), the Conversions API toggle, the encrypted access token, an optional Test Event Code, the catalog toggle, feed token and brand. The tenant bootstrap exposes only meta_pixel_id, meta_debug_mode and meta_server_events_enabled to the storefront. Admin page "تشخيص تكامل ميتا" checks the token, sends a test PageView, shows the delivery log with retry for failed Purchases, lists the feed URLs, validates the catalog and checks ID consistency. Storefront debugging: the debug setting or ?meta_debug=1 logs every Pixel call and relay request in the console. Commerce Manager can only fetch a public HTTPS feed URL. Plan, deploy steps and acceptance checklist: docs/META_PIXEL_AND_CAPI_PLAN.md.
